rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports can be reconciled: the Prophet first visited the charm without removing it, then had it extracted after pain returned, and the pain ceased.
rows.anchor: ويجمع بأنه أتاها صلى الله عليه وسلم بنفسه الشريفة فلم يخرجه ثم إنه وجد بعض الألم فأرسل إليه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that magic made the Prophet imagine he had done things he had not, until God disclosed the matter to him.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت : سحر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أنه ليخيل إليه

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
rows.claim: Zayd reports that a Jewish man bewitched the Prophet by tying a charm and placing it in a well, as Gabriel revealed.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم رضي الله عنه قال : كان رجل يدخل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
rows.claim: The charm was retrieved and untied; the Prophet felt relief with each knot and recovered without confronting or rebuking the man. A variant names Ali and says the water had yellowed.
rows.anchor: فاستخرجوها فجيء بها فحلها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم , فجعل كلما حل عقدة وجد لذلك خفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protection through the two refuge surahs given to the Prophet is also a grace extended to his entire community.
rows.anchor: وهذا الفضل لمنفعة المعوذيتن كما منح الله به رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكذا تفضل به على سائر أمته

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن خبيب
rows.claim: The Prophet instructed reciting al-Ikhlas and both refuge surahs three times morning and evening; Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi grade it hasan sahih, al-Nasa'i transmits it connected or mursal, and al-Nawawi says its chains are sound.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن خبيب رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ) اقرأ قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many reports praise these three surahs, and placing refuge in two surahs signals that seeking it should be repeated.
rows.anchor: والأحاديث في فضل هذه السور الثلاث كثيرة جدا , وجعل التعويذ في سورتين إشارة إلى استحباب تكريره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eleven verses encourage abundant repetition; al-Falaq's five verses pair fittingly with al-Nas's six and follow the preceding odd-numbered surah.
rows.anchor: وجعلتا إحدى عشرة آية ندبا إلى تكثيره في تكريره , وقدمت الفلق التي خمس آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's sublime purpose is seeking God's protection through His nurturing lordship from created harm, magic, and envy; Rabb implies beneficence, nurturing, bringing blessings, and repelling calamities.
rows.anchor: وحاصل هذه السورة العظمة في معناها الأبدع الأسمى الاستعاذة بالله بذكر اسمه { الرب } المقتضي للإحسان والتربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Falaq echoes al-Baqara as the second surah from the end matching the second from the beginning, especially in recalling the Prophet's envying enemies and God's blessings on them.
rows.anchor: كما كان أكثر البقرة المناظرة لها في رد المقطع على المطلع لكونها ثانية من الأول كما أن هذه ثانية من الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magic was among the gravest forms of Jewish misguidance and harm to the Prophet, and the two refuge surahs were revealed in response to it.
rows.anchor: وكان من أعظم ما ضلوا به السحر المشار إليه بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara 2:102 links the Israelites' sorcery to separating spouses, while 2:109 links the People of the Book's envy to wishing believers would abandon faith.
rows.anchor: واتبعوا ما تتلو الشياطين على ملك سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envy in 2:109 supplies a specific parallel: many People of the Book wished to return believers to unbelief out of their own envy.
rows.anchor: ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفرا حسدا من عند أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has twenty-three words, symbolically matching the twenty-third year of prophethood, when the religion was completed, the Prophet died, and the envious lost hope of harming him.
rows.anchor: هي ثلاث وعشرون كلمة إشارة إلى أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم في السنة الثالثة والعشرين من النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding its five pronouns gives twenty-eight, which he associates with 15 AH and Umar's second caliphal year, when campaigns against Persia and Rome weakened hypocrites and envious opponents.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها لاضمائر وهي خمسة كانت ثماني وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the four basmala words gives thirty-two, which he associates with 19 AH, the conquests of Caesarea and Jalula, and the humiliation of Rome and Persia.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضم إليها أربع كلمات البسملة كانت اثنتين وثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counting from the Hijra also evokes the fall of the Persian kings: after the king tore the Prophet's letter and ordered Badhan to attack, God foretold his death; the report arrived as predicted and Badhan and the Persian converts in Yemen embraced Islam.
rows.anchor: فأخبر الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بأنه يقتله سبحانه في ليلة سماها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah seeks refuge in the true God from inward evil; human beings are prone to deceit, and whispering appeals to desires, making its familiar, inward evil especially apt for this surah.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الاعتصام بالإله الحق من شر الخلق الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nas is connected both to uns, since its root is anas, and to naws, inner agitation; these senses make the surah's name fit its subject.
rows.anchor: والناس مشتق من الأنس ، فإن أصله أناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose follows from the Fatiha's watchfulness: the opening and closing surahs frame befriending God and opposing Satan, with the end joined to the beginning as effect to cause.
rows.anchor: ومقصود هذه السورة معلول لمقصود الفقاتحة الذي هو المراقبة ، وهي شاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, Allah encompasses knowledge of inward and outward things, the Merciful's grace reaches all, and the Compassionate completes blessings for His allies throughout their affairs.
rows.anchor: المحيط علما بكل باطن كإحاطته بكل ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah seeks refuge in the true God from inward evil; human beings are prone to deceit, and whispering appeals to desires, making its familiar, inward evil especially apt for this surah.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الاعتصام بالإله الحق من شر الخلق الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nas is connected both to uns, since its root is anas, and to naws, inner agitation; these senses make the surah's name fit its subject.
rows.anchor: والناس مشتق من الأنس ، فإن أصله أناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose follows from the Fatiha's watchfulness: the opening and closing surahs frame befriending God and opposing Satan, with the end joined to the beginning as effect to cause.
rows.anchor: ومقصود هذه السورة معلول لمقصود الفقاتحة الذي هو المراقبة ، وهي شاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, Allah encompasses knowledge of inward and outward things, the Merciful's grace reaches all, and the Compassionate completes blessings for His allies throughout their affairs.
rows.anchor: المحيط علما بكل باطن كإحاطته بكل ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Falaq first seeks broad protection from bodily and other harms affecting all creation, then names specific dangers; its external misfortunes and inward faults are both included, though bodily calamity is most evident.
rows.anchor: لما جاءت سورة الفلق للاستعاذة من شر ما خلق من جميع المضار البدنية وغيرها العامة للإنسان وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy is the gravest of the named calamities, and envy was the root of the enmity between jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: وختمت بالحسد فعلم أنه أضر المصائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nas addresses the narrower evil of whispering, which underlies inward flaws and all sins; it is more potent when coming from jinn.
rows.anchor: جاءت سورة الناس متضمنة للاستعاذة من شر خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like al-Falaq, the surah includes a command, an act of seeking refuge, the one sought for protection, and the evil sought against.
rows.anchor: فقد تضمنت السورة كالفلق استعاذة ومستعاذا به ومستعاذا منه وأمرا بإيجاد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sought as Rabb because lordship best fits protection, aid, care, creation, governance, nurture, and reform, with complete power, mercy, generosity, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: لما كانت صفة الربوبية من صفات كماله سبحان أليق بالحماية

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Rabb means the one who owns, brings and preserves good, repels evil, raises the dependent toward perfection, and governs by preservation and completion.
rows.anchor: قال الملوي : والرب من له ملك الرق وجلب الخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase Rabb al-nas suits harms that afflict rational human and jinn souls, whereas al-Falaq concerns bodily harms shared by humans and other creatures.
rows.anchor: وخص الإضافة بالمزلزلين المضطربين في الأبدان والأديان من الإنس والجان لخصوص المستعاذ منه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr explains the order as general followed by specific: al-Falaq leaves the dangers broad or indefinite, while al-Nas identifies and describes the particular enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : وجه تأخرها عن شقيقتها عموم الأولى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He says beginning with the general and then specifying it more fully better achieves the aim of seeking protection, as with the distinction between Rahman and Rahim.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بالمعموم ثم أتبع بالخصوص ليكون أبلغ في تحصيل ما قصدت الاستعاذة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb suggests gentleness and nurture, while Malik conveys domination, sovereignty, and justice; since Rabb may not itself imply kingship or complete disposal, the order begins with Rabb and follows with Malik.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الرب الملك متقاربين في المفهوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik signals complete disposal, effective power, and full sovereignty, making God the refuge, helper, one invoked for aid, and final resort.
rows.anchor: وإليه المفزع وهو المستعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a king need not be a deity and divinity admits no partner, Ilah is the culmination: God alone is their deity, just as He alone is their Lord and King.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الملك قد لا يكون إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran argues from people’s admission that God alone is Lord and King to the worship they deny: they should worship and seek refuge only in Him.
rows.anchor: هذه دائما طريقة القرآن يحتج عليهم بإقرارهم بتوحيدهم له في الربوبية والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deity is manifest through subtle acts of care that make people love, trust, and seek Him, yet hidden by majesty beyond their comprehension, inspiring both longing and fear.
rows.anchor: والإله من ظهر بلطيف صنائعه التي أفادها مفهوم الرب والملك في قلوب العباد فأحبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the explicit word al-nas instead of using pronouns renews the reminder of humanity's agitation and need before each name's sign of absolute sufficiency, and honors human beings through added clarification.
rows.anchor: وكرر الاسم الظاهر دون أن يضمر فيقول مثلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated explicit noun also prevents any divine name from being restricted to the preceding possessive relation; each attribute is universal in its own right.
rows.anchor: ولئلا يظن أن شيئا من هذه الأسماء يتقيد بما أضيف غليه الذي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refuge gathers every aspect of lordship, kingship, and divinity; the variation among attributes is treated like variation among essences to stress the gravity of the danger.
rows.anchor: واندرج في هذه الاستعاذة جميع وجوه الاستعاذات من جميع وجوه التربية وجميع الوجوه المنسوبة إلى المستعيذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no conjunction between the names because the refuge is sought through their combined attributes on one essence, as though they were one attribute.
rows.anchor: ولم يعطف بالواو لما فيها من الإيذان بالمغايرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb comes first for its universal scope; Ilah comes last because disobedience excludes a person from acknowledging God as deity; Malik stands between them as ruler who commands and forbids.
rows.anchor: وقدم الربوبية لعمومها وشمولها لكل مربوب على حد سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kingship follows creation and completes lordship, while true divinity completes kingship; thus lordship entails kingship and kingship entails divinity.
rows.anchor: وملكه لهم تابع لخلقه إياهم فملكه من كمال ربوبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three relations encompass the foundations of faith and divine names: Rabb includes creative power, reform, and mercy; Malik covers command and majesty; Ilah gathers all perfection and majesty.
rows.anchor: وقد اشتملت هذه الإضافات الثلاث على جميع قواعد الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb gathers the attributes of beauty needed for reform and mercy, Malik the names of command and majesty, and Ilah all attributes of perfection; their fullness makes the seeker worthy to seek refuge.
rows.anchor: والملك هو الآمر الناهي المعز المذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence is an ascent of recognition: blessings reveal a nurturer, knowledge reveals the self-sufficient King, and His unique governance after creation reveals the sole deserving deity.
rows.anchor: لأن من رأى ما عليه من النعم الظاهرة والباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers omit the alif in Malik here, unlike the Fatiha; Malik of people implies their kingship, while reading Mālik would lessen the intended force of the title.
rows.anchor: فقد أجمع القراء في هذه السورة على إسقاط الألف من { ملك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different spelling in Āl ʿImran suits its context of God granting or withholding sovereignty, where Mālik is more apt.
rows.anchor: وأطبقوا في آل عمران على إثبات الألف في المضاف وحذفها من المضاف إليه لأن المقصود بالسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswas is a verbal noun like zilzal; it denotes the whisperer by his habitual act, intensifying the description, and means covert, repeated casting of meanings into the heart.
rows.anchor: هو اسم بمعنى الوسوسة كالزلزال بمعنى الزلزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled sound of waswasa suits repeated, covert whispering; its source evokes jewelry, inner speech, and dogs' murmuring, and its verbal noun is waswas with kasra, as in 33:11.
rows.anchor: وأصلها صوت الحلي , وحديث النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn tempter can move through a human like blood through the body, as reported in the Sahih.
rows.anchor: والموسوس من الجن يجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan secretly ornaments sin and stirs desire until a person commits it, then urges others to expose the sinner, whose shame can make him bolder.
rows.anchor: فهو يوسوس بالذنب سرا ليكون اجلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tempter makes people emulate their natural inclinations toward vice; pride and self-admiration are the most destructive roots, as they destroyed Satan.
rows.anchor: وشره التحبيب إلى الإنسان بما يميل إليه طبعه حتى يشاكله في رذيلة الطبع وظلمة النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride breeds malice and envy, rejection of truth and sin, and contempt for people, echoing Satan's claim that he was better than Adam in 7:12.
rows.anchor: وينشأ من الكبر الحقد والحسد يترشح منه بطر الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contempt grows into disrespecting God's allies, withholding their rights, assaulting and oppressing them, as implied by Satan's words in 7:12.
rows.anchor: ومنه تنشأ الاستهانة بأولياء الله تعالى بترك احترامهم ومنع حقوقهم والاعتداء عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malice produces withholding good and harmful speech and action; envy corrupts relationships and produces lying and deception, as shown in 7:20–21.
rows.anchor: وترشح من الحقد الذي هو العداوة العظيمة إمساك الخير والإحسان وبسط اللسان واليد بكل سوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-admiration produces resentment of God's decree and using analogy against revelation, as illustrated by Satan's objections in 17:61 and 15:33.
rows.anchor: ويترشح عن الإعجاب التسخط للقضاء والقدر كما آذن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance and defiance lead to external corruption of beliefs, morals, deeds, bodies, and livelihoods; repeated vice becomes entrenched like Satan, while Adam's lapse was remediable because his nature was good.
rows.anchor: والإذلال وهو الجرأة على المخالفات فينشأ عن ذلك شرور متعدية , وهي السعي في إفساد العقائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God is the cure for whispering: it drives Satan away and illuminates and purifies the heart.
rows.anchor: وكان قد جعل دواء الوسوسة ذكره سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannas means one who repeatedly withdraws and hides; Satan retreats when a person remembers God and resumes whispering when remembrance stops.
rows.anchor: أي الذي عادته أن يخنس أي يتوارى ويتأخر ويختفي بعد ظهوره مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance strikes down the corrupter, who is intensely repelled by it; a report from some early Muslims likens a believer to thinning his camel by wearing down Satan.
rows.anchor: فالذكر له كالمقامع التي تقمع المفسد

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi describes Satan with a dog's-trunk-like proboscis in a person's chest.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : له خرطوم كخرطوم الكلب في صدر الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative description gives Satan a serpent's head by the heart, whispering there; it withdraws at God's remembrance and returns when remembrance ceases.
rows.anchor: ويقال : رأسه كرأس الحية واضع رأسه على يمين القلب يحدثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuwaswisu means secretly and repetitively casting harmful meanings so they reach understanding without being heard; the chest is named as the heart's arena and dwelling.
rows.anchor: أي يلقي المعاني الضارة على وجه الخفاء والتكرير بحيث تصل مفاهيمها من غير سماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chest is the heart's entryway: reason establishes true premises, but when it pauses before a conclusion the imaginative faculty resumes whispering, which darkly congenial nature accepts.
rows.anchor: فإنها دهاليز القلوب منها تدخل الواردات إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon says al-nas can mean humans and jinn; its roots may be anas, movement or agitation (naws), or forgetfulness (nisyan).
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس : يكون من الإنس ومن الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final phrase warns that whisperers include both jinn and humans, with jinn named first because they are more harmful; it may also explain the word people.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الذي يعلم الإنسان الشرة تارة من الجن وأخرى من الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn are intensely evil, rebellious, and hidden; people are unstable and wavering, whether the reference is to humans or jinn.
rows.anchor: من الجنة } أي الجن الذين في غاية الشر والتمرد والخفاء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says a jinn tempter can whisper to other jinn just as jinn whisper to humans.
rows.anchor: ويوسوس له - قاله الغوي عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending returns to the opening by explaining the people bearing God's attributes; thoughts may be divine inspiration, angelic inspiration, satanic whispering, or self-talk, with inspiration in the heart and whispering in the chest.
rows.anchor: وقد ختمت السورة بما بدئت به , والمعنى الثاني أوفق برد آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Watchfulness repels harmful incoming thoughts; without it, they overrun and master a person.
rows.anchor: فإن كان الإنسان مراقبا دفع عن نفسه الضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Test thoughts against religious law and priority: even lawful acts should wait if they would displace a greater virtue; for worldly concerns, deliberate, consult someone trustworthy in faith and reason, then seek istikhara.
rows.anchor: فإن وافق الشرع فلينظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish inspirations by inward response: divine inspiration brings an open chest and calm, whereas satanic or egoic thoughts constrict the chest and unsettle the self, supported by a Prophetic report on virtue and sin.
rows.anchor: وقد جعل بعضهم قانون الخاطر الرحماني أن ينشرح له الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A satanic thought urges any sort of disobedience and may vanish with remembrance; an egoic thought remains fixed on a particular benefit or harm and does not recede through remembrance.
rows.anchor: ويعرف الشيطاني بالحمل على مطلق المخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human tempters among spouses, children, and friends may be more harmful than jinn; the remedy is separation and distance as far as possible.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون الشيطان إنسيا من أزواج وأولاد ومعا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The author cites the Arab group calling themselves people of jinn as an example supporting al-Farra on the term al-nas.
rows.anchor: قالوا : أناس من الجن , قال : وهذا معنى قول الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For choosing companions, al-Kahf 18:28 is a major rule: stay with those who call on God and do not follow one whose heart has forgotten Him and follows desire.
rows.anchor: واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nas joins the Fatiha and closes the Quran by matching its names: the Fatiha has Allah, Rabb, and Malik, while al-Nas has Rabb, Malik, and Ilah.
rows.anchor: أن الفاتحة اشتملت على ثلاثة أسماء : الله والرب والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha's unique name Allah and al-Nas's declaration of the true deity make the Quran's ending return to its beginning without any partner in divinity.
rows.anchor: واختصت الفاتحة بالاسم الذي لم يقع فيه شركة أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining the ending to the opening yields the sequence Ilah, Malik, Rabb, Allah, Rabb, Rahman, Rahim, Malik, portraying God as deity and sovereign who creates, nurtures, and gives general and special mercy.
rows.anchor: فيصير النظم إذا ألصفت آخر الناس بأول الفاتحة ( إله ملك رب الله رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nas seeks refuge from whispering in the chest that yields vigilance, while the Fatiha empties the inner self of distraction for exclusive attention to God, the highest watchfulness.
rows.anchor: وحاصل سورة الناس الاستعاذة بهذا الرب الموصوف من وسوسة الصدر المثمرة للمقرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God helps, refuge makes trust sincere and the servant becomes an instrument of divine hearing, sight, hand, and foot; nearness should increase worship until death ends Satan's deception, as 15:99 commands.
rows.anchor: فإذا أراد الحق إعانة عبد حمله على الاستعانة بالاستعاذة فيسر عليه صدق التوكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet encouraged beginning the Quran again after completing it, calling the practice al-hall al-murtahil; the surah's ending therefore prompts refuge before a new recitation.
rows.anchor: وقد ندب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى افتتاح القرآن بعد ختمه كما أشار إليه اتصال المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeking refuge at the close, the reader begins with the basmala, which is required to keep watchfulness at every beginning and end.
rows.anchor: استعذ يا من ختم القرآن العظيم لتفتتحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala may be understood as part of what is said after qul, attached either to a'udhu or to Rabb al-nas.
rows.anchor: أو أن البسملة مقول في { قل } على سبيل من { أعوذ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Refuge repels harm while naming God attracts good; because God commands seeking refuge when reciting the Quran, it belongs at the beginning and relates to the Fatiha as effect to cause.
rows.anchor: والتسمية أمر بالدفع والجلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the only Lord, King, and deity, praised for encompassing all things and able to aid; His name denotes a perfect attribute or the set of His beautiful attributes.
rows.anchor: فإن الاسم هو الوصف والمراد به الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker relies on God's complete attributes because every need requires power, knowledge, or generosity, all of which belong to Him.
rows.anchor: فإن البدءل فيه يحتاج إلى قدرة , فله القدرة التامة , أو إلى علم فالعلم صفته , أو كرم فكذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge through God's comprehensive, unmatched name asks for broad mercy and then the special mercy that brings the deficient servant to divine pleasure and exclusive worship.
rows.anchor: خصوصا صفة الرحمة العامة التي شملتني أكنافها , وأقامني إسعافها , ثم الرحمة الخاصة التي أنا أجدر الناس باستمطارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing three surahs match the opening three in aims: al-Ikhlas corresponds to Ali Imran in affirming oneness, al-Falaq to al-Baqara, and al-Nas to the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: لما قرب التقاء نهاية الدائرة السورية آخرها بأولها ومفصلها بموصلها اشتد تشاكل الرأسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preparing the chest by removing inward evil readies it for the Fatiha's watchfulness; the argument links 2:67, 2:102, and 2:109 to al-Falaq and al-Nas.
rows.anchor: والناس للفاتحة , فإنه إذا فرغ الصدر الذي هو مسكن القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reader begins with the familiar, simple refuge but at the end is granted protection against every aberrant union; this recalls the lesson for people of understanding.
rows.anchor: وكأنه اكتفى أولا بالاستعاذة المعروفة كما يكتفي في أوائل الأمور بأيسر مأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twenty words of al-Nas symbolically match 7 AH and the Pilgrimage of Fulfillment, countering Satan's whisper around the earlier Hudaybiyya vision of entering the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: فهي عشرون كلمة توازيها إذا حسبت من أول النبوة سنة عمرة القضاء وهي السابعة من الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding three pronouns gives twenty-three words, matching 10 AH and the Farewell Pilgrimage; the report that Satan despaired of Arabian worship was fulfilled when Abu Bakr defeated the apostasy.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها الضمائر الثلاث كانت ثلاثا وعشرين فوازت السنة العاشرة من الهجرة وهي سنة حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet said Satan had despaired of being worshiped in Arabia after that day.
rows.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حجة الوداع ( إن الشيطان قد أيس أن يعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the basmala words gives twenty-seven, matching 14 AH and Umar's ascendancy, when Satan avoided the path Umar took.
rows.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها كلمات البسملة صارت سبعا وعشرين توازي سنة استحكام أمر عمر بن الخطاب الفاروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Satan takes another path whenever Umar takes one.
rows.anchor: الذي ما سلك فجا إلا سلك الشيطان فجا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together the Fatiha and al-Nas use twenty-six of the Arabic letters: eighteen are shared, and each has four distinct letters; Ibn Milq separately says seven letters are absent from the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: انتظمت من ستة وعشرين حرفا وهي ما عدا الثاء المثلثة والزاء الظاء المعجة

rows.speaker: ابن ميلق
rows.claim: Ibn Milq says seven letters are absent from the Fatiha; the author speculates that the letter counts of the first and last surahs symbolize twenty-two years of revelation and a twenty-third year of meeting God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن ميلق : سقط من الفاتحة سبعة أحرف ( ثج خز شظف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqa'i completed the first draft in 875 AH after beginning in 861 AH, then completed the fair copy in Damascus in 882 AH, marking fourteen and twenty-two years of work.
rows.anchor: فرغته في المسودة يوم الثلاثاء سابع شعبان سنة خمس وسبعين وثمانمائة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says that after nearly half the work was done, envious critics attacked him for using Torah and Gospel material; he defended this as a sound practice supporting Islam and cited al-Shafi'i, al-Nawawi, and al-Rafi'i.
rows.anchor: دب داء الحسد في جماعة أولي النكد , والمكر واللدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports commissioning learned scholars to write the opinions collected in his Maṣāʿid al-naẓar, after which God exposed and humiliated his critics.
rows.anchor: فصنفت في ذلك الأقوال القويمة , في حكم النقل من الكتب القديمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqa'i says opponents next challenged him over an innovation and he wrote a response arguing that their position opposed Quran and Sunna and the Shafi'i tradition.
rows.anchor: ثم قاموا في بدعة دائم المعروف , فصنفت فيها القول المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes opponents promoting Ibn al-Farid and the doctrine of union, stirring public hostility; a few supporters remained, and his question left the opponents unable to answer.
rows.anchor: ثم قاموا في فتنة ابن الفارض , وكلهم معاند معارض , وألبوا علي رعاع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He lists polemical works against Ibn al-Farid and Ibn Arabi and the doctrine of union, and says a later reply was confused, wrong throughout, explicitly unbelieving in four places, and false in eight.
rows.anchor: منها ( صواب الجواب للسائل المرتاب ) ومنها ( القارض لتكفير ابن الفارض ) ومنها ( تدمير المعارض في تكفير ابن الفارض )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqa'i says God sustained his patience through years of hardship until he completed the book in the form he judged excellent and sound.
rows.anchor: وثبت الله ورزق الصبر والأناة حتى أكمل هذا الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the title Kitab Lima through the work's central aim: each sentence should connect to what precedes it, the meaning and spirit that give speech its life beyond isolated word meanings.
rows.anchor: لأن جل مقصوده بيان ارتباط الجمل بعضها ببعض حتى أن كل جملة تكون آخذة بحجزة ما أمامها متصلة بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says لما acts like a condition joining two clauses, requiring the second to follow firmly from the first, which is why he used it repeatedly in this work.
rows.anchor: و ( لما ) طرف يراد بها ثبوت الثاني مما دخل عليه بثوبت الأول على غاية المكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his concluding poem, al-Biqa'i asks God and the Prophet to protect the book from an envious detractor, whose effort to disparage it will turn to ruin while the book gains honor and success.
rows.anchor: أعيذه بالمصطفى من شر وغد ذما ومن حسود قد غدا من أجله مهتما

rows.speaker: خليل بن موسى المقرئ
rows.claim: A student praises the book as a proof that unveils Quranic secrets and claims no later commentator can match it.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض تلامذة المصنف وهو العرس خليل بن موسى المقرئ مادحا للكتاب المذكور المسمى ب ( لما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies himself as al-Biqaʿi and describes himself as needing forgiveness from God.
rows.anchor: قال ذلك منشبه أحوج الخلائق إلى عفو الخالق أبو الحسن إبراهيم بن عمر بن حسن الرباط
